unit_judgments.rationale: The draft mentions this sentence only as context on C0000 and C0001, but did not create an explicit claim covering the goal to obtain the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained.
quotes: The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0000, which reflects that infant eyes may be partially or completely closed.
quotes: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0001, allowing discreet support of an infant's head.
quotes: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0002, stating that head tilt is acceptable for infants.
quotes: Head tilt is acceptable for infants;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0003, prohibiting a parent's face from appearing in an infant photograph.
quotes: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0004, requiring a new photograph if requirements are not met.
quotes: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0005, specifying that the photograph must be in color.
quotes: The photograph must be in color;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0006, specifying the recommendation for photo age within six months and likeness.
quotes: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0007, permitting hairstyle or facial hair changes if likeness is maintained.
quotes: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

unit_judgments.rationale: The note regarding re-using passport photographs from naturalization/citizenship certificates was not extracted as a claim in the draft.
quotes: Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization. Be aware that even if the certificate itself was recently issued, because of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services processing times, the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0008, requiring photographs to be free of material damage.
quotes: The photograph must be free of material damage:

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0009, defining material damage.
quotes: Material damage is any damage to the facial area that makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes);

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0010, defining immaterial damage.
quotes: Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes).

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0011, establishing that immaterial damage is acceptable.
quotes: Immaterial damage is acceptable;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0012, exempting applicants from signing the photograph.
quotes: The applicant does not need to sign the photograph, as this often causes creases or smudges;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0013, requiring acceptance agents to sign the back of hand-carry photographs.
quotes: For hand-carry applications, the acceptance agent signs the back of the photograph.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0014, permitting the return of an application to adjudication to request a new photo if defects appear upon printing.
quotes: Consequently, the passport application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph even though the photograph appeared acceptable.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0015, prohibiting eyeglasses except where medically unremovable.
quotes: Eyeglasses are not acceptable unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons, e.g., the applicant has recently had ocular surgery and the eyeglasses are necessary to protect the applicant’s eyes.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0016, requiring a signed medical statement when eyeglasses cannot be removed.
quotes: A medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner must be requested in these rare circumstances.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0017, prohibiting eyeglass frames from covering the eye(s).
quotes: The frames of the eyeglasses must not cover the eye(s);

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0018, prohibiting glare obscuring the eye(s).
quotes: There must not be glare on eyeglasses that obscures the eye(s);

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0019, prohibiting shadows or refraction obscuring the eye(s).
quotes: There must not be shadows or refraction from the eyeglasses that obscure the eye(s); and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered fully by C0020, permitting dark or tinted lenses when required by the medical statement.
quotes: Dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement also indicates that they are required.
